findings: Correcting the target did not rescue the axis. With the exact per-row settlement value as the learning target, the combiner still fails: hard selection scores 0.597643 on Q3 and 0.638385 on Q4 against the deployed 0.605136 and 0.641831, and the shrunk variant converges to the deployed blend (0.641855 versus 0.641831 on Q4).
The combiner overwhelmingly selects D or the blend (5428 of 6408 rows pick D on Q3), which is the correct conservative behaviour and confirms it is not simply mis-trained.
Value-argmax accuracy is 0.617978 on Q3 and 0.389957 on Q4 over five candidates, so the model does carry information about which candidate is better, yet that information does not convert into Total.
Two independent target formulations now fail identically: error rank in N41 and exact settlement value here. The replicated negative supports a single conclusion.
reinterpretation: The +0.094 per-row oracle headroom measured in N40 is an ORACLE ARTIFACT of selecting on the realized outcome, not accessible signal. Which member happens to land inside the 6 percent band on a given row is dominated by the realization, not by anything observable at D-1 14:00. FD14 and FD15 are therefore closed together.
residual_deficit: FD12 remains the only measured axis still open at its root: every member is built on the same 820-column collapsed representation, so all four share the same over-dispersed conditional density. A genuinely sharper, better-calibrated density has never been built locally.
